# mcp-mail — full documentation

<!-- README.md -->

# mcp-mail

**mcp-mail is a self-hosted IMAP/SMTP email MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any other MCP client read, search, draft and send email from your existing mailbox, with per-client permissions, an audit log and a one-line install.**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Annseraf/mcp-mail/main/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --auto-update
```

Local clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code) can run it directly: `npx -y @annseraf/mcp-mail stdio`.

mcp-mail is a maintained continuation of [claude-mail-mcp](https://github.com/maxx3250/claude-mail-mcp) by Markus Stöger (MIT). Existing claude-mail-mcp v0.2 installs can switch with **no config changes** ([compatibility contract](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md)).

## Works with

- **AI clients:** Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT (developer mode, deep research), Cursor, VS Code, Meta Muse, and any MCP client over Streamable HTTP or stdio. Setup guides: [docs/clients](docs/clients/).
- **Mail providers:** any IMAP/SMTP mailbox: Fastmail, iCloud, Purelymail, Gmail and Google Workspace (app password), Yahoo, Zoho, Mailbox.org, Migadu, Mailcow, Dovecot/Postfix.
- **Calendars:** any CalDAV server (Fastmail, iCloud, Nextcloud, Radicale), optional.
- **MCP protocol:** 2026-07-28 (stateless) and every earlier revision since 2024-11-05, on the same endpoint.

## Tools

| Tool                                              | What it does                                                                               | Capability             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- |
| `list_accounts`                                   | List connected mailboxes, sender names and signatures (never credentials)                  | read                   |
| `list_folders`                                    | List folders with their special use (Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Trash)                           | read                   |
| `list_messages`                                   | Newest messages in a folder, with short previews                                           | read                   |
| `search_messages`                                 | Search one folder, several, or all (`"*"`) by sender, subject, body, date, read or flagged | read                   |
| `get_message`                                     | Read one message: headers, body, attachment list, threading ids                            | read                   |
| `get_attachment`                                  | Download one attachment (size-capped)                                                      | read                   |
| `get_thread`                                      | Read a whole conversation across Inbox and Sent, oldest first                              | read                   |
| `list_threads`                                    | Group a folder's newest messages into conversations                                        | read                   |
| `create_draft`                                    | Save a draft (with attachments); `reply_to_uid` fills in the reply for you                 | draft                  |
| `mark_read`                                       | Mark a message read or unread                                                              | organize               |
| `set_flags`                                       | Star (flag), mark answered, or add custom keywords                                         | organize               |
| `move_message`                                    | Move a message to another folder                                                           | organize               |
| `delete_message`                                  | Move to Trash; `permanent: true` deletes for good                                          | organize / destructive |
| `send_message`                                    | Send an email (with attachments and signature); a copy goes to Sent                        | send                   |
| `update_account_settings`                         | Change the sender display name and signature                                               | settings               |
| `list_calendars`, `list_events`, `find_free_slot` | Read calendars and find free time                                                          | calendar-read          |
| `create_event`                                    | Create a calendar event                                                                    | calendar-write         |
| `search`, `fetch`                                 | ChatGPT deep research adapters (`CHATGPT_COMPAT=true`)                                     | read                   |

## Comparison

|                                     | **mcp-mail**                                                                  | claude-mail-mcp v0.2               |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Transport                           | Streamable HTTP (2026-07-28 + legacy) and stdio                               | Streamable HTTP                    |
| Auth                                | Built-in OAuth 2.1 (DCR, PKCE), per-client tokens, shared token               | Shared token + separate OAuth shim |
| Per-client permissions              | Presets, tool allow/deny, mailbox scope, recipient allowlist, send rate limit | —                                  |
| Read-only mode                      | `read-only` preset (or `STDIO_PRESET=read-only`)                              | —                                  |
| Revoke one client                   | Yes, others keep working                                                      | Rotate the shared secret           |
| Attachments                         | Send, draft and download                                                      | Send only                          |
| Threads, flags, multi-folder search | Yes                                                                           | —                                  |
| Audit log                           | JSONL, no message content                                                     | —                                  |
| Prompt-injection hygiene            | Untrusted-content fencing, hidden-HTML stripping, server instructions         | —                                  |
| Multi-tenant + admin API            | Opt-in, with OpenAPI spec                                                     | —                                  |
| Install and updates                 | One-line installer, signed releases, auto-update with rollback                | Manual                             |

Other IMAP MCP servers worth a look, depending on your needs: [codefuturist/email-mcp](https://github.com/codefuturist/email-mcp) (TypeScript, IMAP/SMTP, many tools), [tecnologicachile/mail-mcp](https://github.com/tecnologicachile/mail-mcp) (Rust, IMAP/SMTP plus Microsoft Graph and EWS) and [wildsurfer/your-mail-mcp](https://github.com/wildsurfer/your-mail-mcp) (read-only, local notmuch index). Check their READMEs for current features.

## FAQ

### How do I give ChatGPT read-only access to my email?

Run `mcp-mail clients add chatgpt --for chatgpt` (OAuth login, `read-only` preset), enable `OAUTH=true`, and add the server in ChatGPT's developer mode. ChatGPT only ever sees the read tools. See [docs/clients/chatgpt.md](docs/clients/chatgpt.md).

### Can I use this with Fastmail, iCloud, Purelymail or Gmail?

Yes. Anything that speaks IMAP and SMTP works. For Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo and Fastmail, create an app password in the provider's security settings and use it instead of your normal password.

### How do I stop an AI agent from sending email?

Give the agent a preset without `send` (`read-only`, `read-draft` or `organize`). The send tool then disappears from its tool list and is rejected if called anyway. For agents that may send, restrict recipients with `sendRecipientAllowlist` and cap volume with `sendRateLimit`. See [docs/CLIENTS.md](docs/CLIENTS.md).

### Can an email trick the AI into doing something?

Emails are untrusted input. mcp-mail wraps every body in untrusted-content delimiters, strips hidden HTML text and tracking pixels, and tells clients to confirm sends and deletions with you. Keep sending off for agents that don't need it. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

### Does deleting a message lose it forever?

No. `delete_message` moves the message to Trash. Permanent deletion needs `permanent: true` and a client with the `destructive` capability.

### Where are my passwords stored?

In `accounts.json` on your server (optionally encrypted at rest with `mcp-mail secrets encrypt`). In multi-tenant mode, credentials are envelope-encrypted per tenant with a local key file or OCI Vault. They are never returned by any tool, API or log.

### Can my agent sign emails?

Yes. Each account can have a sender display name and a signature, set in `accounts.json` or by the agent itself with `update_account_settings`. Pass `include_signature: false` to send without it.

### I'm on claude-mail-mcp. Do I need to change anything?

No. Swap the binary; your `.env`, `accounts.json` and connected clients keep working. CI enforces this against recorded v0.2.1 behavior.

## Security model

- Binds to `127.0.0.1` by default; put nginx or Caddy in front for TLS.
- Clients authenticate with OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, rotating refresh tokens), per-client static tokens (stored hashed), or the legacy shared token.
- Every tool call is checked against the client's policy twice: when listing tools and when calling them.
- The audit log records who did what, never message content.
- Mail content is fenced as untrusted; sends and deletions should be confirmed by a human.
- Releases are built by CI from tagged commits only, with checksums and provenance attestation.

Details: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [docs/CLIENTS.md](docs/CLIENTS.md), [docs/PLATFORM.md](docs/PLATFORM.md).

## Configuration

- `.env`: transport settings ([.env.example](.env.example)). Everything new is optional.
- `accounts.json`: mailboxes (same format as claude-mail-mcp; optional `fromName`/`signature`).
- `clients.json`: per-client identities and policies ([docs/CLIENTS.md](docs/CLIENTS.md)).
- Multi-tenant mode and the admin API: [docs/PLATFORM.md](docs/PLATFORM.md).

## Upgrading

From claude-mail-mcp v0.2.x: **no config changes required.** Install mcp-mail pointing at the same `.env`, `accounts.json` and (if you use one) OAuth state. New features stay off until you enable them. Two approved behavior changes are listed in [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md#intentional-deviations): deleting moves to Trash, and email content is fenced as untrusted (`UNTRUSTED_FENCING=false` restores the old output).

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run check        # lint, format, typecheck, unit tests, license scan, build
npm run test:compat  # compatibility gate + integration suites (needs GreenMail, see docs/COMPATIBILITY.md)
```

Adding a tool: [docs/ADDING_A_TOOL.md](docs/ADDING_A_TOOL.md). Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Client setup guides

| Client                       | Transport                    | Auth         | Guide                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Claude.ai (web, mobile)      | Remote HTTP                  | OAuth login  | [claude-ai.md](claude-ai.md)                     |
| Claude Desktop / Claude Code | stdio (local) or remote HTTP | none / token | [claude-desktop-code.md](claude-desktop-code.md) |
| ChatGPT                      | Remote HTTP                  | OAuth login  | [chatgpt.md](chatgpt.md)                         |
| Cursor                       | stdio or remote HTTP         | none / token | [cursor.md](cursor.md)                           |
| VS Code (Copilot agent mode) | stdio or remote HTTP         | none / token | [vscode.md](vscode.md)                           |
| Meta Muse                    | Remote HTTP                  | token        | [muse.md](muse.md)                               |
| Anything else                | Remote HTTP or stdio         | token        | [generic.md](generic.md)                         |

Remote HTTP needs mcp-mail reachable over HTTPS (`https://mail.example.com/mcp` below). Create
one client per agent with `mcp-mail clients add <id> --for <type>` so each gets its own
permissions and can be revoked on its own ([CLIENTS.md](../CLIENTS.md)).

<!-- docs/clients/claude-ai.md -->

# Claude.ai

Claude.ai connects to remote MCP servers that support OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration.

1. On the server, enable OAuth and create a login for Claude:
   ```sh
   # .env
   OAUTH=true
   TOKEN_SECRET_FILE=/etc/mcp-mail/token-secret   # openssl rand -hex 32 > ...
   ```
   ```sh
   mcp-mail clients add claude --for claude --preset read-draft
   # prints a username and password once
   ```
2. In Claude.ai: **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**.
   - Name: `Email`
   - URL: `https://mail.example.com/mcp`
3. Click **Connect**. A sign-in page from your server opens; use the username and password from
   step 1. Claude returns to the chat with the connector enabled.

To let Claude send mail, use `--preset full-no-delete`, and consider `sendRecipientAllowlist`
in `clients.json`. Revoke at any time with `mcp-mail clients revoke claude`.

---

<!-- docs/clients/claude-desktop-code.md -->

# Claude Desktop and Claude Code

## Local (stdio), simplest

mcp-mail runs as a child process and reads `~/.config/mcp-mail/accounts.json` (or `ACCOUNTS_FILE`).

Claude Desktop, `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "email": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@annseraf/mcp-mail", "stdio"],
      "env": {
        "ACCOUNTS_FILE": "/Users/you/.config/mcp-mail/accounts.json",
        "STDIO_PRESET": "read-draft"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add email -e STDIO_PRESET=read-draft -- npx -y @annseraf/mcp-mail stdio
```

`STDIO_PRESET` is optional (`read-only`, `read-draft`, `organize`, `full-no-delete`, `full`).

## Remote (HTTP)

```sh
mcp-mail clients add claude-code --for generic --preset read-draft   # prints a token once
claude mcp add --transport http email https://mail.example.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

---

<!-- docs/clients/chatgpt.md -->

# ChatGPT

Checked against OpenAI's documentation on 2026-11-02.

ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers in **developer mode** (Settings → Apps → Advanced) using
OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. mcp-mail implements RFC 9207 issuer
identification, so ChatGPT uses its stable callback
`https://chatgpt.com/connector_platform_oauth_redirect`, which is in the default
`ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS`.

1. Server:
   ```sh
   # .env
   OAUTH=true
   TOKEN_SECRET_FILE=/etc/mcp-mail/token-secret
   CHATGPT_COMPAT=true        # adds read-only `search` and `fetch` for deep research
   ```
   ```sh
   mcp-mail clients add chatgpt --for chatgpt     # read-only preset, OAuth login printed once
   ```
2. In ChatGPT: **Apps → + → Add custom MCP server**, URL `https://mail.example.com/mcp`,
   authentication **OAuth**. Sign in with the login from step 1.
3. After changing presets or tools, press **Refresh** on the app so ChatGPT re-reads the tool list.

Notes:

- Deep research and company knowledge only use tools named `search` and `fetch`; mcp-mail's
  versions search Inbox and Sent of every account and return fenced message text.
- Read tools carry `readOnlyHint`, so ChatGPT runs them without asking; anything else needs your
  confirmation in the conversation.
- Write tools (drafts, sending) depend on your ChatGPT plan's developer-mode support.

---

# Cursor

`~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "email": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@annseraf/mcp-mail", "stdio"],
      "env": { "STDIO_PRESET": "read-draft" }
    }
  }
}
```

Remote server instead:

```sh
mcp-mail clients add cursor --for cursor     # token printed once
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "email": {
      "url": "https://mail.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- docs/clients/vscode.md -->

# VS Code (Copilot agent mode)

`.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "email": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@annseraf/mcp-mail", "stdio"],
      "env": { "STDIO_PRESET": "read-draft" }
    }
  }
}
```

Remote server (`mcp-mail clients add vscode --for vscode` prints a token):

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    { "id": "mailToken", "type": "promptString", "description": "mcp-mail token", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "email": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mail.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:mailToken}" }
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- docs/clients/muse.md -->

# Meta Muse

Checked 2026-11-02 against public setup guides; Meta's own documentation is still sparse.

Muse has no "add MCP server" setting. You ask it in chat to build a **Custom Connector**; it
writes an MCP client on its cloud VM, tests it and saves it as a skill. The server must be
public HTTPS speaking Streamable HTTP (a localhost or stdio server is unreachable from Muse).
A static bearer token is the smoothest auth.

1. Create a token client:
   ```sh
   mcp-mail clients add muse --for muse          # read-draft preset, token printed once
   ```
2. In Muse, send:
   > Build a Custom Connector that acts as an MCP client for my email.
   > Server URL: https://mail.example.com/mcp
   > Transport: remote streamable HTTP
   > Auth: HTTP header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. I'll paste the token in the secure
   > credential prompt, not in chat.
3. Paste the token only into Muse's secure credential prompt.

Muse can then list, search and read mail and save drafts. Grant `send` only if you need it.

---

<!-- docs/clients/generic.md -->

# Any MCP client

**Remote (Streamable HTTP).** `POST https://mail.example.com/mcp` with
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (from `mcp-mail clients add <id> --for generic`). Both
2026-07-28 (stateless, per-request `_meta`) and initialize-based clients work.

```sh
curl -s https://mail.example.com/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -H "MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

**Local (stdio).** `npx -y @annseraf/mcp-mail stdio`, with `ACCOUNTS_FILE` and optional `STDIO_PRESET`.

Clients that only support OAuth sign-in can use the built-in OAuth server (`OAUTH=true`); see
[claude-ai.md](claude-ai.md).

---

<!-- docs/CLIENTS.md -->

# Clients, OAuth, policies and audit

Every feature on this page is opt-in. With no `clients.json`, `OAUTH` unset and `AUDIT_LOG`
unset, mcp-mail behaves exactly like claude-mail-mcp v0.2.x.

## Identities

A request to `/mcp` is identified as one of:

| Credential                           | Client                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The shared `AUTH_TOKEN`              | Built-in `legacy` client with full access (override it with a `clients.json` entry whose id is `legacy`) |
| An OAuth access token (`OAUTH=true`) | Matched to a client by OAuth client id, then by login user; unmatched logins get `defaultPolicy`         |
| A per-client static token            | Matched by its SHA-256 hash in `clients.json`                                                            |

## clients.json

Next to `accounts.json`, or wherever `CLIENTS_FILE` points. Changes apply without a restart.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "defaultPolicy": "read-draft",
  "clients": [
    { "id": "claude", "match": { "oauthUser": "claude" }, "preset": "full-no-delete" },
    {
      "id": "muse",
      "match": { "tokenHash": "sha256:…" },
      "preset": "read-draft",
      "accounts": ["main"]
    },
    {
      "id": "assistant",
      "match": { "tokenHash": "sha256:…" },
      "preset": "full-no-delete",
      "denyTools": ["create_event"],
      "sendRecipientAllowlist": ["@example.com", "boss@example.org"],
      "sendRateLimit": { "perHour": 10 }
    }
  ]
}
```

Policies grant capabilities, not tool names, so new tools are governed automatically:

| Preset           | Capabilities           | Tools                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `read-only`      | read, calendar-read    | list/search/get messages, folders, accounts, calendars, events, free slots |
| `read-draft`     | + draft                | + `create_draft`                                                           |
| `organize`       | + organize             | + `mark_read`, `move_message`, `delete_message` (to Trash)                 |
| `full-no-delete` | + send, calendar-write | + `send_message`, `create_event`                                           |
| `full`           | + destructive          | + `delete_message` with `permanent: true`                                  |

Enforcement has two layers: tools a client may not use are left out of its `tools/list`, and
every call is checked again at dispatch. `allowTools` / `denyTools` override the preset.

## Managing clients

```sh
mcp-mail clients add claude --for claude --preset full-no-delete   # OAuth login, password shown once
mcp-mail clients add muse --for muse --accounts main               # static token, shown once
mcp-mail clients list
mcp-mail clients rotate muse      # new token; the old one stops working at once
mcp-mail clients revoke muse      # this client only; others keep working
```

`--for` picks the auth mode and a default preset: `claude` (OAuth, read-draft), `chatgpt`
(OAuth, read-only), `cursor`, `vscode`, `muse`, `generic` (token, read-draft). Only token hashes
and scrypt password hashes are stored.

## Built-in OAuth 2.1

`OAUTH=true` serves OAuth discovery, dynamic client registration, `/authorize` with a login page
(PKCE S256 required), `/token` (rotating refresh tokens), `/revoke`, and protected-resource
metadata. `/mcp` then answers unauthenticated requests with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge so
clients like Claude.ai can discover it.

| Variable                                   | Meaning                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TOKEN_SECRET[_FILE]`                      | HMAC key for access tokens, hex, at least 32 characters |
| `LOGIN_USER`, `LOGIN_PASSWORD_HASH[_FILE]` | Primary login (`scrypt:N:r:p:salt:hash`)                |
| `OAUTH_USERS_FILE`                         | More logins (written by `clients add --auth oauth`)     |
| `OAUTH_STATE_FILE` (or `STATE_FILE`)       | Registered clients and hashed refresh tokens            |
| `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS`                    | Comma-separated; defaults to Claude.ai's callbacks      |

It reads and writes the same token, state and password formats as the reference OAuth shim, so
an existing shim deployment can point these variables at its current values and connected
clients keep working without reconnecting (see [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md)).

Revoking a client invalidates its tokens immediately; rotating an OAuth client sets a new
password and signs out its existing sessions. Neither affects other clients.

## Audit log

`AUDIT_LOG=/var/log/mcp-mail/audit.jsonl` (or `stdout`) writes one JSON line per tool call:
timestamp, client, tool, account, mailbox, UID, recipient count for sends, result
(`ok`/`denied`/`error`), denial reason and duration. Bodies, subjects, attachments, passwords and
tokens are never logged. The file rotates at 5 MB.

```sh
mcp-mail audit tail --client muse -n 50
```

## Deleting messages

`delete_message` moves the message to the account's Trash folder (found by its `\Trash`
special-use flag or a conventional name). `permanent: true` deletes it for good and needs the
`destructive` capability.

---

<!-- docs/COMPATIBILITY.md -->

# Compatibility contract

Anyone running claude-mail-mcp v0.2.x must be able to swap in mcp-mail with **zero config
edits**, and connected MCP clients (including Claude.ai custom connectors) must keep working
**without reconnecting**. This document is the contract, and CI enforces it.

## What must not change

| Surface               | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Environment variables | Every v0.2.x variable keeps its name, meaning and default. New variables are optional and default to v0.2.x behavior.                                                                                                                       |
| `accounts.json`       | `"version": 1` files load forever, from the same default path or `ACCOUNTS_FILE`. New fields are optional. Unknown fields are tolerated. The file is never rewritten unless you run an explicit migration command, which backs it up first. |
| Tool names            | All 14 v0.2.x tools keep their exact names.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Tool inputs           | Additive only. New parameters are optional. A parameter is never made required, removed, or narrowed (type, enum, bounds, pattern, format). Relaxing is fine.                                                                               |
| Tool outputs          | Additive only. No field is renamed, removed or retyped.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| HTTP surface          | `POST /mcp` (Bearer `AUTH_TOKEN`) and `GET /health` keep their paths and behavior.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Protocol              | Clients that use the `initialize` handshake (protocol revisions 2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25) keep working alongside newer revisions.                                                                                                      |
| OAuth continuity      | Deployments that front the server with the reference OAuth shim keep their registered clients, refresh tokens, access tokens and login (see below).                                                                                         |

## How it is enforced

`npm run test:compat` (CI job "Compatibility gate") builds the server, starts it against a
throwaway [GreenMail](https://greenmail-mail-test.github.io/greenmail/) IMAP/SMTP server, and:

1. Compares `tools/list` with the recorded baseline in `compat/baseline/<ref>/tools-list.json`.
   It fails on a removed tool, a newly required parameter, a removed parameter, or any
   narrowing of a parameter's accepted values.
2. Replays a fixed scenario of tool calls (all 14 tools, both accounts, error paths) and
   compares the JSON shape of every output with `compat/baseline/<ref>/outputs.json`. It fails
   if a field disappears or changes type, or if a call starts or stops erroring.
3. Replays the same scenario as a 2026-07-28 client (no handshake, per-request `_meta`) against
   the same baseline, and checks `server/discover`, header validation (`-32020`) and version
   negotiation (`-32022`).
4. Runs `initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call` for every legacy protocol revision, checks
   that legacy responses are plain JSON, Bearer auth, and overlapping concurrent requests.

Unit tests (`npm test`) also load the golden v0.2.1 `accounts.json` and `.env` files in
`compat/fixtures/upstream-v0.2.1/`, and pin the OAuth shim formats in
`compat/fixtures/oauth-shim-v0.1/`.

### Run it locally

```sh
docker run -d --name greenmail -p 127.0.0.1:3025:3025 -p 127.0.0.1:3143:3143 \
  -e GREENMAIL_OPTS='-Dgreenmail.setup.test.smtp -Dgreenmail.setup.test.imap -Dgreenmail.hostname=0.0.0.0 -Dgreenmail.users=alice:alicepw@example.com,bob:bobpw@example.com -Dgreenmail.users.login=email' \
  greenmail/standalone:2.1.5
npm run test:compat
```

Point the harness at another server with `COMPAT_MAIL_HOST`, `COMPAT_IMAP_PORT` and
`COMPAT_SMTP_PORT`.

### Baselines

Baselines are recorded from a git ref, never from the code under test:

```sh
npm run compat:baseline -- v0.2.1
```

This builds the ref in a temporary worktree and replays the same scenario. Re-record only when
the scenario itself changes (for example to cover a new tool), and review the diff: a baseline
change that drops or narrows anything is a contract change.

## OAuth shim formats

Existing deployments may run the reference OAuth 2.1 shim in front of `/mcp`. Its state must
remain valid when mcp-mail's built-in OAuth replaces it:

- **Access tokens:** `base64url(JSON) "." base64url(HMAC-SHA256(first part, TOKEN_SECRET))`,
  payload `{ typ: "at", cid, scp, aud, exp }`, 1 hour lifetime.
- **Refresh tokens:** random, stored as the SHA-256 hex of the token in `state.json` under
  `refresh`, with `{ cid, scp, aud, exp }`; 30 days; rotated on use.
- **Clients:** RFC 7591 dynamic registrations in `state.json` under `clients`, keyed by `client_id`.
- **Login:** `LOGIN_USER` plus `LOGIN_PASSWORD_HASH` in the form `scrypt:N:r:p:<salt>:<hash>`
  (base64url).
- **Paths:** OAuth discovery metadata, `/register`, `/authorize`, `/token`, `/revoke`, `/login`,
  and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

## Intentional deviations

Approved by the maintainer; the tool schemas and output fields stay compatible.

| Change                                                                                                                                                                                      | Why                                                      | Opt out                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `delete_message` moves the message to Trash; permanent deletion needs `permanent: true` (and the `destructive` capability when a client policy applies)                                     | Reversible by default                                    | Pass `permanent: true`    |
| Email bodies and previews are wrapped in `<untrusted_email_content>` delimiters, HTML-only mail is converted with hidden text and images removed, and outputs gain a `content_notice` field | Prompt-injection hygiene ([SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)) | `UNTRUSTED_FENCING=false` |
| Calendar tools say "No calendar (CalDAV) is connected…" instead of pointing to a `/settings` page                                                                                           | The old text referred to a UI this project doesn't ship  | none                      |

Everything else is additive: new optional parameters, new tools, new output fields.

---

<!-- docs/PLATFORM.md -->

# Platform mode: multi-tenant engine and admin API

mcp-mail runs in two shapes from the same code:

- **Self-hosted (default).** One mailbox owner, `accounts.json`, one `/mcp` endpoint. Nothing on
  this page is active unless you turn it on, and behavior is identical to claude-mail-mcp v0.2.x
  (enforced by the [compatibility gate](COMPATIBILITY.md)).
- **Platform mode (opt-in).** Many tenants, each with their own mailboxes, agent clients,
  limits and audit log, managed by a product through a private admin API.

All extension points below are generic: any self-hoster or product can use them.

## MCP protocol support

Every MCP endpoint serves both protocol eras on the same URL:

| Client                                                                                | How it's served                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-07-28 (stateless, per-request `_meta`, `server/discover`)                        | SDK v2 strict handler: header validation (`-32020`), version negotiation (`-32022`) |
| 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25 (`initialize` handshake, e.g. existing Claude.ai connectors) | Stateless, plain JSON responses, exactly as v0.2.x                                  |

## Settings

| Variable                                              | Default              | Meaning                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MULTI_TENANT`                                        | `false`              | Serve `POST /t/<tenantId>/mcp`                                                         |
| `DATA_DIR`                                            | `/var/lib/mcp-mail`  | Tenants, encrypted secrets, audit logs                                                 |
| `TENANT_BASE_URL`                                     | `PUBLIC_URL`         | Public origin used in endpoint URLs, e.g. `https://connect.example.com`                |
| `CONFIG_PROVIDER`                                     | `store`              | `store` (admin API manages tenants) or `http` (an internal service owns tenant config) |
| `CONFIG_PROVIDER_URL`, `CONFIG_PROVIDER_TOKEN[_FILE]` |                      | For `http`: `GET <url>/tenants/<id>` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`              |
| `CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_MS`                                 | `30000`              | Cache TTL for `http` config                                                            |
| `SECRETS_KEY_PROVIDER`                                | `local`              | `local` (key file) or `oci` (OCI Vault)                                                |
| `SECRETS_KEY_FILE`                                    | `$DATA_DIR/keys/kek` | 32-byte key-encryption key, mode 0600                                                  |
| `ADMIN_API`                                           | `false`              | Serve `/admin/v1` (requires `MULTI_TENANT=true`)                                       |
| `ADMIN_HOST` / `ADMIN_PORT`                           | `127.0.0.1` / `3330` | Must be loopback or a private address; public binds are refused                        |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN[_FILE]`                                  |                      | Service token, at least 32 characters                                                  |
| `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION`                                  | unset                | Single-tenant only: `local` decrypts `enc:v1:` passwords in `accounts.json`            |

## Tenants

A tenant record holds limits, mailboxes (hosts, ports, users, display names) and agent clients.
It never holds secrets: mailbox passwords live in the secret store and client tokens are stored
only as SHA-256 hashes.

**Isolation.**

- A client token is only ever checked against the tenant named in the URL, so a token for
  tenant A fails on tenant B's endpoint. Unknown tenants and bad tokens get the same `401`.
- Account ids resolve only within the tenant, and within the client's allowed mailboxes.
- IMAP/SMTP connections, decrypted credentials, rate counters and audit logs are per tenant.
- Deleting a tenant closes its connections, deletes its secrets and data key, audit log, usage
  counters and record.

**Limits** (pushed by the product, enforced by the engine): `maxMailboxes`, `maxClients`,
`toolCallsPerDay`, `allowSend`, `maxRecipientsPerSend`, `auditRetentionDays`. A suspended tenant's
agents get "This account is suspended" on every tool call.

**Client policy.** Each client has a preset that grants capabilities; tools a client may not use
are hidden from `tools/list` and rejected if called anyway. Sending additionally needs the
tenant's `allowSend` and the client's own `sendEnabled` toggle, which is off by default.

| Preset           | Capabilities                 |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `read-only`      | read, calendar-read          |
| `read-draft`     | + draft                      |
| `organize`       | + organize (mark read, move) |
| `full-no-delete` | + send, calendar-write       |
| `full`           | + destructive (delete)       |

## Secret store

Envelope encryption: each tenant has a random 256-bit data key; secrets are sealed with
AES-256-GCM under it (bound to tenant and secret name), and the data key is stored only wrapped
by a key-encryption key (KEK) from a key provider. Secrets can be set or replaced through the
admin API but never read back through any API, log, error or tool output.

Key providers:

- **`local`**: a KEK file. Create it with `mcp-mail secrets init-key --key-file <path>`. Keep it
  on a different volume from `DATA_DIR`, readable only by the engine user.
- **`oci`**: OCI Vault master key via the crypto endpoint's `encrypt`/`decrypt` with API-key
  request signing. Set `OCI_KMS_CRYPTO_ENDPOINT`, `OCI_KMS_KEY_ID`, `OCI_TENANCY_OCID`,
  `OCI_USER_OCID`, `OCI_KEY_FINGERPRINT`, `OCI_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`. The signing is unit-tested
  against OCI's documented scheme; validate against your Vault before production use.

Other KMSs implement the two-method `KeyProvider` interface in `src/platform/secrets.ts`.

**Single-tenant encryption at rest** (opt-in): `mcp-mail secrets encrypt` rewrites the password
fields of `accounts.json` as `enc:v1:…` values after writing a timestamped backup; then set
`SECRETS_ENCRYPTION=local` and `SECRETS_KEY_FILE`. `mcp-mail secrets decrypt` reverses it.

## Admin API

`/admin/v1`, specified in [`openapi/admin-v1.json`](../openapi/admin-v1.json). Every response in
the integration suite is validated against the spec, and CI fails if any operation is untested.
Breaking changes ship as `/admin/v2`, with v1 kept for at least one major version.

| Area      | Operations                                                                               |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tenants   | create, get, suspend, unsuspend, delete (purge), set limits                              |
| Mailboxes | list, add, update (incl. password replacement), remove, test connectivity without saving |
| Clients   | list, add (returns endpoint + token once), update, revoke, rotate                        |
| Activity  | audit log (paginated, filter by client), usage per day and client                        |
| Meta      | health, version                                                                          |

A minimal product-side client is in [`examples/admin-client.mjs`](../examples/admin-client.mjs).

## Audit log

One JSONL line per tool call per tenant (`$DATA_DIR/audit/<tenant>.jsonl`, rotated at 5 MB):
timestamp, client, tool, account, mailbox, UID, recipient count for sends, result
(`ok`/`denied`/`error`), denial reason and duration. Message bodies, subjects, attachments,
passwords and tokens are never logged.

## `/version`

Public on every deployment: package version, commit SHA, build time and (for CI-built images)
the container image digest, so anyone can match a running deployment to a public commit.

## OAuth for tenant endpoints (delegated login)

Clients that can only connect through a browser sign-in (Claude.ai, ChatGPT) use OAuth. With
`TENANT_OAUTH=true` each tenant gets its own issuer at `<TENANT_BASE_URL>/t/<tenant>/`. The
engine has no user accounts, so the login step is handed to the product:

1. The client discovers OAuth from the 401 challenge on `/t/<tenant>/mcp`, registers (DCR) and
   opens `/t/<tenant>/authorize`.
2. The engine redirects the browser to `OAUTH_DELEGATE_URL` with `txn` (signed, 10 minutes),
   `tenant`, `client_name`, `redirect_host` and `return_to`.
3. The product signs the user in, checks they own the tenant, picks or creates the agent client
   (admin API `POST /tenants/<id>/clients`), and redirects to
   `return_to?txn=<txn>&client=<client id>&sig=<hex HMAC-SHA256(OAUTH_DELEGATE_SECRET, "<txn>.<client id>")>`.
   To refuse: `error=access_denied&sig=<HMAC of "<txn>.denied">`.
4. The engine issues tokens bound to that tenant and agent client. Revoking or rotating the
   client signs the session out.

| Variable                       | Meaning                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TENANT_OAUTH`                 | `true` to enable (requires `MULTI_TENANT`)                                 |
| `TENANT_TOKEN_SECRET[_FILE]`   | Master key, 64+ hex characters; each tenant's token key is derived from it |
| `OAUTH_DELEGATE_URL`           | The product's login/consent page                                           |
| `OAUTH_DELEGATE_SECRET[_FILE]` | Shared HMAC secret, 32+ characters                                         |
| `TENANT_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` | Optional; defaults to Claude.ai's and ChatGPT's callbacks                  |

Discovery follows RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 path insertion
(`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/t/<tenant>`,
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/t/<tenant>/mcp`) and is also served under
`/t/<tenant>/.well-known/…`. Each tenant has its own token key, state file and resource URL, so a
token for one tenant never works on another. Deleting a tenant removes its OAuth state.

## Not yet in platform mode

Single-tenant OAuth and `clients.json` policies are described in [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md).

<!-- SECURITY.md -->

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Until v1.0, only the latest minor release is supported with security fixes.

| Version | Supported                                                |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0.2.x   | yes                                                      |
| 0.1.x   | no — upgrade to 0.2.1 (see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)) |

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public GitHub issue for security problems.**

Preferred channel:

1. **GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting** — open a private advisory at
   <https://github.com/maxx3250/claude-mail-mcp/security/advisories/new>

Alternative channel:

2. Email **security@markusstoeger.com**. PGP is not required.

## What to include

- A description of the issue and its impact
- Steps to reproduce (or a proof of concept)
- The affected version / commit
- Whether the issue is already public anywhere

## Response timeline

- **Acknowledgement** within 48 hours
- **Initial assessment** within 7 days
- **Fix or status update** within 14 days

If the report is valid, a fix is published as a patch release and a GitHub Security Advisory with a CVE (where applicable) is opened. Reporters are credited unless they request otherwise.

## Threat model

**Assets we protect:**

- Mailbox credentials (IMAP/SMTP/CalDAV passwords in `accounts.json`)
- Email content (read access, write access, deletion)
- Calendar data
- The Bearer token gating `/mcp`
- The OAuth signing key

**Adversaries we consider:**

- Random internet attacker (port scan, brute force)
- Malicious page loaded in the operator's browser (CSRF against `/settings`)
- Compromised network path between Claude.ai and the connector (MITM)
- A compromised Claude.ai client (malicious tool calls)
- Local-system attacker (other processes on the same host)

**Out of scope:**

- A root-level compromise of the host. With root, all credentials are recoverable from `/var/lib/mail-mcp/accounts.json` — same security boundary as `~/.ssh/id_rsa` or `/etc/shadow`. We do not attempt at-rest encryption that depends on a key also stored on the same host.
- Compromise of the upstream mailbox provider.
- Phishing of the operator's htpasswd login.

## What this project does

### Transport

- TLS terminated by nginx, certificate from Let's Encrypt (90-day rotation by `certbot.timer`).
- HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on every response.
- Backend and OAuth shim bound to `127.0.0.1` only. systemd kernel-level network filter (`IPAddressDeny=any`, `IPAddressAllow=127.0.0.1/32`) on the shim as a backstop.

### Authentication

- OAuth 2.1 + Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) + PKCE (S256).
- JWT access tokens (RS256, 1h TTL), refresh tokens (30d, stored as SHA-256 hashes).
- Human login via htpasswd; brute-force throttled by nginx (`limit_req`, 10 req/min per IP).
- `/settings` UI gated by HTTP Basic Auth against the same htpasswd file.
- `/settings` POST endpoints additionally protected by Origin/Referer CSRF guard.

### Process isolation

- Both processes (backend + shim) run as the dedicated non-root `mailmcp` system user (no shell, no home directory).
- systemd hardening: `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome`, `PrivateTmp`, `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectKernel*`, `ProtectControlGroups`, `ProtectClock`, `ProtectHostname`, `ProtectProc=invisible`, `RestrictNamespaces`, `RestrictRealtime`, `RestrictSUIDSGID`, `LockPersonality`, `SystemCallFilter=@system-service ~@privileged @resources`.
- Writable filesystem limited to `/var/lib/mail-mcp` (state dir).
- Memory and task caps via `MemoryMax`, `TasksMax`, `LimitNOFILE`.

### Credentials at rest

- `accounts.json` and `token` files are owned by `mailmcp:mailmcp` and chmod 600.
- `.env` is `root:mailmcp` 640 (root can edit, the service can read).
- htpasswd file is `root:mailmcp` 640 (not world-readable).

### Input validation

- Every MCP tool input validated with [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas.
- `accounts.json` schema-validated on every load (id pattern, port ranges, required fields).
- `/settings/save` re-validates all fields and rejects bad input with a redirect.
- Subprocess invocations (`htpasswd -vb`) use `execFile` (no shell) with a regex-gated username (`[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}`) and a length-bounded password.

### Output filtering

- `list_accounts` returns id/label/default/From/imap_host/caldav_enabled — never credentials.
- `/health` shows the same public summary.
- Server logs never include passwords or Bearer tokens.

## Hardening checklist for operators

These are not vulnerabilities in this project, but operators should:

- [x] Run behind HTTPS with a valid certificate (the included nginx vhost + certbot does this).
- [x] Bind the Node processes to `127.0.0.1` and let nginx handle public traffic.
- [x] Run the systemd units as a dedicated non-root user.
- [x] Use a host firewall (UFW or equivalent) with default-deny incoming.
- [ ] Rotate `AUTH_TOKEN` periodically. Restart both services after rotation.
- [ ] Use app-specific passwords on providers that support them — never your main account password.
- [ ] Restrict who can reach the connector at the network level (VPN, IP allowlist, or htpasswd in front of the OAuth shim).
- [ ] Run a fail2ban jail against the shim's auth-fail log lines (`[oauth-shim] login fail` and `[oauth-shim] settings auth fail`) for additional brute-force protection.
- [ ] Keep `accounts.json` out of any backups that leave the host unencrypted.
- [ ] Subscribe to GitHub Security Advisories for this repo and the dependencies (`imapflow`, `nodemailer`, `tsdav`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`).

See [docs/HARDENING.md](docs/HARDENING.md) for the full operator checklist and threat-model walkthrough.

## Prompt injection (mcp-mail)

Anyone can email you, so every email body is untrusted input for the agent reading it. mcp-mail
reduces the risk in layers:

- **Fencing (default on):** bodies, previews and thread contents are wrapped in
  `<untrusted_email_content>` delimiters with a note that the content is data, not instructions.
  Delimiters inside a message are neutralized. Disable with `UNTRUSTED_FENCING=false`.
- **Clean HTML:** HTML-only mail is converted to text with hidden elements (`display:none`,
  zero-size or white-on-white text, `hidden`), scripts, styles and images (tracking pixels)
  removed; links are shown as text with their target, so nothing is fetched automatically.
- **Server instructions:** clients receive instructions to treat email as data and to confirm
  sends and deletions with the user.
- **Least privilege:** give agents only the capabilities they need (`clients.json` presets,
  docs/CLIENTS.md). Sending can be limited by recipient allowlist and rate; permanent deletion
  needs an explicit capability.

None of this makes an agent immune: keep humans in the loop for sends and deletions.

<!-- docs/INSTALL.md -->

# Installing and updating

## One-line install (Ubuntu / Debian, systemd)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Annseraf/mcp-mail/main/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --auto-update
```

| Option              | Meaning                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--auto-update`     | Daily update check (randomized time), same major version only             |
| `--domain <host>`   | Also configure nginx and a Let's Encrypt certificate (`--email` optional) |
| `--port <n>`        | Backend port for a fresh install (default 3220)                           |
| `--version <x.y.z>` | Install a specific version                                                |
| `--dry-run`         | Show what would happen                                                    |
| `--uninstall`       | Remove the program; keeps config and mailbox data                         |

The installer is idempotent. It installs Node.js 22 if needed, creates the `mailmcp` system user,
writes `/etc/mcp-mail/mcp-mail.env` (with a generated `AUTH_TOKEN`) only if it doesn't exist, and
runs mcp-mail as a hardened systemd unit (`mcp-mail.service`) on `127.0.0.1`.

**Adopting claude-mail-mcp.** If a `claude-mail-mcp.service` unit exists, the installer reuses its
`EnvironmentFile`, user, port, accounts file and keys, starts `mcp-mail.service` with them, and
disables the old unit only after the new one passes its health check. Nothing is moved or
regenerated. To go back: `systemctl disable --now mcp-mail && systemctl enable --now claude-mail-mcp`.

## Layout

| Path                                | Contents                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/opt/mcp-mail/releases/<version>/` | Unpacked releases (the three newest are kept)                 |
| `/opt/mcp-mail/current`             | Symlink to the running release                                |
| `/opt/mcp-mail/bin/mcp-mail-update` | Updater                                                       |
| `/usr/local/bin/mcp-mail`           | CLI (runs with the service's settings)                        |
| `/etc/mcp-mail/mcp-mail.env`        | Settings (fresh installs)                                     |
| `/var/lib/mcp-mail/`                | `accounts.json`, `clients.json`, OAuth state (fresh installs) |
| `/var/log/mcp-mail/`                | `audit.jsonl`, `update.log`                                   |

## Updates

```sh
mcp-mail update --check          # current vs newest in the same major version
sudo mcp-mail update --now       # update now
sudo mcp-mail update --now --major
sudo mcp-mail update --enable-auto | --disable-auto
mcp-mail version
```

Every update:

1. downloads the release tarball, `SHA256SUMS` and a Sigstore bundle from GitHub Releases;
2. verifies the checksum and that the signature was made by this repository's release workflow
   (`cosign verify-blob` with a pinned cosign);
3. unpacks it next to the current release and switches the `current` symlink;
4. restarts the service and runs `mcp-mail doctor --live`: `/health` must answer and `tools/list`
   must still contain every tool in the compatibility snapshot;
5. on any failure, switches back, restarts and logs to `/var/log/mcp-mail/update.log`.

**Supply-chain trade-off.** Auto-update means trusting new releases from this repository. Releases
are built only by GitHub Actions from tagged commits (never from a laptop), signed keylessly with
Sigstore and published with build-provenance attestations, and auto-update never crosses a major
version. If you would rather review each release, leave `--auto-update` off and run
`mcp-mail update --check` yourself.

## Docker

```sh
docker run -d --name mcp-mail -p 127.0.0.1:3220:3220 \
  -e AUTH_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32) -v mcp-mail-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/annseraf/mcp-mail:1
```

Images are multi-arch (amd64, arm64) with provenance attestations
(`gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/annseraf/mcp-mail:1 --repo Annseraf/mcp-mail`).

## Local clients

`npx -y @annseraf/mcp-mail stdio`; see [clients/claude-desktop-code.md](clients/claude-desktop-code.md).

<!-- docs/ADDING_A_TOOL.md -->

# Adding a tool

Tools are registered in `src/tools-mail.ts` (mail) or `src/tools-calendar.ts` (calendar). Every
tool gets client policy, auditing, annotations and server instructions for free: the guard and
annotation wrappers sit in front of `registerTool`. You only declare the tool and its capability.

Example: `count_unread` (a read-only tool), 30 lines.

```ts
// 1. src/policy/capabilities.ts — declare exactly one capability
export const TOOL_CAPABILITY = {
  // ...
  count_unread: "read",
};

// 2. src/imap-client.ts — the provider method (keep IMAP details here)
async countUnread(mailbox: string): Promise<number> {
  const client = await this.ensureConnected();
  const status = await client.status(mailbox, { unseen: true });
  return status.unseen ?? 0;
}

// 3. src/tools-mail.ts — inside registerMailTools()
server.registerTool(
  "count_unread",
  {
    description: "Count unread messages in a folder.",
    inputSchema: z.object({
      mailbox: z.string().optional().describe("Folder (default INBOX)"),
      account: accountSchema,
    }),
  },
  async ({ mailbox, account }) => {
    const { imap } = pool.for(account);
    return asJson({ mailbox: mailbox ?? "INBOX", unread: await imap.countUnread(mailbox ?? "INBOX") });
  },
);
```

Then:

- Add a test in `test/platform/mail-tools.int.test.ts` (runs against GreenMail).
- Treat message content as untrusted: wrap bodies with `fence()` from `src/content.ts`.
- Never add a required parameter to an existing tool or remove an output field; the
  compatibility gate (`npm run test:compat`) fails if you do.
